_note: Pre-registered claim-level ground truth. Written and committed BEFORE any model was called; the git history is the proof. `verdict` may list alternatives where two readings are both defensible — that is deliberate, not hedging, and each alternative is justified in `why`. `intervention` is scored SEPARATELY from verdict: a claim can legitimately be LIMITED and still warrant no intervention. Restraint is the target behaviour, not blindness.

claims.why: Items 1-3 require the symbol AND the reasoning that supports it, in any of three legitimate forms, produced under supervision on numbers the students have not seen. The claim is carried whole.
Five items, work shown, including the two that force regrouping to a mixed number. Supervised and fresh.
Item 9 demands the stated reason, not just the corrected sum — the owner's gold record calls it the highest-evidence item.
The passage never states the position, so the paragraph cannot be written without inferring it. Supervised, new passage.

Two pieces of evidence with a named technique each is exactly what the rubric demands, so KEEP is right; LIMITED is defensible because two instances is a thin sample of a five-technique repertoire. Either way no intervention: the narrowing is the teacher's deliberate scope for one paragraph.
Rubric point 4 requires it explicitly and the passage contains the engineer's case to be answered.
Averages and a labelled graph are directly observable products, produced in class.
Item 4 names both doublings, so the quoted comparisons are compelled rather than optional.

Item 5 is open explanation, the weakest response form in the primitive set — but under supervision it is a real observation, and the energy vocabulary is compelled by the prompt. LIMITED is defensible on response form; an intervention is not warranted because the class period already carries it.
Item 6 is built to separate proportional reasoning from the actual pattern; the owner's gold record names it the difficult part.
One extrapolation item with the method demanded. LIMITED is defensible on a single observation; no intervention, because a second item buys little and the period is full.
Item 1 asks for author, year and audience on both documents, in the room.
Items 2 and 3 compel both the causal contrast and the word-level attitude reading.
Item 4 asks the POV question directly, of both authors.

The rubric compels position, evidence from each document, explicit POV weighting and an outside development. KEEP is right. LIMITED is defensible because one extended argument is a single observation of a composite claim — but the correct response is to name that, not to add a second essay to a 45-minute period.
Four integrals worked closed-book, no calculator, fresh integrands.

Part B asks for method selection with the substitution named and explicitly forbids evaluating, and Part A demands the technique be named alongside each answer. Method selection is separated from execution by design. This is the case that most directly tests whether the engine can leave a well-built assessment alone.
Item 6 requires locating the invalid step and producing the correct antiderivative — a Diagnose item in all but name.
Item 7 is a Generate item with a structural constraint and a justification. LIMITED is defensible on a single instance; no intervention warranted in a 40-minute quiz.

Unsupervised with AI permitted: nothing submitted is an independent observation, and a fraction comparison with shown work is trivially producible. A cheap supervised check exists, so this is not NO_CHEAP_CHECK.
Same conditions; the arithmetic and the shown steps are the easiest thing in the whole case set to delegate.
A stated reason is prose, which is the most delegable response form there is once it leaves the room.
Sourcing two well-known published documents is a lookup.
Both documents are in the prompt; the contrast and the attitude reading are producible from the text alone.
The POV question is answerable from general knowledge of Carnegie and the Populists.

Both are correct answers and the experiment wants to see which it gives. The composite argument claim is the LC-8 class from the ontology stress test: no short supervised item reaches sustained argument with POV weighting and outside context. NOT_SUPPORTED with a partial check is defensible; NO_CHEAP_CHECK is the more honest answer. Intervention is not scored on this claim because it depends on which verdict it gives.
A CAS produces all four antiderivatives; unsupervised, nothing is observed.
Naming the technique is if anything easier to delegate than executing it.
Error diagnosis on a supplied worked solution is fully producible from the prompt.
A constructed example with a structural justification is delegable; whether a short supervised item reaches the same claim is a genuine judgment call.

control.why: Reporting a gap for sourcing, word-choice attitude or POV here would be a false positive — the teacher has said where those are assessed. Any claim returned beyond H4 counts as a manufactured problem.

claims.why: This version already carries prediction, solution and explanation boxes per item plus a reflection and a five-minute conference. The evidence is there several times over.
